newsitem.title: USA: CME traders call USDA data bullish for CME bellies.
newsitem.headline: CME traders call USDA data bullish for CME bellies.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange traders called the U.S. Agriculture Department's Cold Storage Report bullish for CME pork belly futures, and said they expect futures to open 0.50 to 2.00 cents per lb higher on Wednesday.
USDA reported frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses totaled 38.032 million lbs as of December 31, the smallest December 31 supply in 10 years.
"The major component was the reduced production during the month," said Chuck Levitt, analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.
USDA reported pork belly supplies increased nearly 7.1 million lbs from November 30 to December 31, versus a 10.5-million-lb monthly increase a year ago.
The 38.032-million-lb supply as of December 31 was near the low-end of analysts' pre-report estimates, which ranged from 37.4 million to 41.5 million.
In addition to reduced production versus a year ago, Levitt said demand for bacon by restaurants continued to be strong.
"The market is going to rally a bit on it but it is old news in a way. The important thing is what happens in February and March," said Rich Tokheim, analyst with Investment Research Co, Omaha.
Tokheim said a year ago there was an out movement from mid-January to March 10 of about 3.0 million lbs. But, he doubts that will be repeated this year because higher prices should ration demand.
CME February pork bellies closed Tuesday at 75.300 cents per lb versus about prices in the mid-50s a year ago.
